marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q001.takeaway: The diaphragm receives superior and inferior phrenic, musculophrenic and pericardiophrenic arterial branches; “middle phrenic” is not a standard supply.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q001.displayText:
The diaphragm receives superior and inferior phrenic, musculophrenic and pericardiophrenic arterial branches; “middle phrenic” is not a standard supply.

The diaphragm is not supplied by a middle phrenic artery. The source lists its arterial supply as superior phrenic arteries, inferior phrenic arteries, musculophrenic arteries, pericardiophrenic arteries, and the lower five intercostal and subcostal arteries.
emphasis: The diaphragm receives superior and inferior phrenic, musculophrenic and pericardiophrenic arterial branches; “middle phrenic” is not a standard supply

rationales.a: Musculophrenic artery supplies the peripheral diaphragm.
rationales.b: Inferior phrenic arteries are major arterial supplies from the abdominal aorta.
rationales.c: Pericardiophrenic artery accompanies the phrenic nerve and supplies diaphragm/pericardium.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q002.takeaway: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon at T8.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q002.displayText:
The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon at T8.

The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm via the caval opening. The source diaphragm diagram also identifies the right phrenic nerve near the caval opening, the esophageal opening, aortic opening and arcuate ligaments.
emphasis: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon at T8

rationales.a: The esophagus passes through the muscular right crus at T10.
rationales.b: The aorta passes posterior to the diaphragm at T12 through the aortic hiatus.
rationales.d: Sympathetic trunks pass posterior to the medial arcuate ligaments rather than through the tendon.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q003.takeaway: The right phrenic nerve accompanies the IVC through the caval opening, labeled 3 in the source diagram.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q003.displayText:
The right phrenic nerve accompanies the IVC through the caval opening, labeled 3 in the source diagram.

The right phrenic nerve passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm, either through the caval hiatus or immediately lateral to it. In the source figure this route is labeled 3. The other labeled structures are 1 - medial arcuate ligament, 2 - aortic opening, and 4 - esophageal opening. The left phrenic nerve passes through the muscular diaphragm anterior to the central tendon and is more anterior than the right. Phrenic-nerve injury during cardiothoracic surgery may cause diaphragmatic paralysis with elevation of the affected hemidiaphragm on chest radiograph.
emphasis: The right phrenic nerve accompanies the IVC through the caval opening, labeled 3 in the source diagram

rationales.a: Label 1 is the medial arcuate ligament, not the caval passage.
rationales.b: Label 2 is the aortic opening, which transmits aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein.
rationales.d: Label 4 is the esophageal hiatus, transmitting esophagus and vagal trunks.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q004.takeaway: The sympathetic trunk passes posterior to the medial arcuate ligament marked A.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q004.displayText:
The sympathetic trunk passes posterior to the medial arcuate ligament marked A.

The area marked A is the medial arcuate ligament. The thoracic sympathetic trunk passes posterior to the medial arcuate ligament and continues into the abdomen as the lumbar sympathetic trunk.
emphasis: The sympathetic trunk passes posterior to the medial arcuate ligament marked A

rationales.a: The right phrenic nerve passes through the caval foramen/central tendon, not behind the medial arcuate ligament.
rationales.c: The vagus nerve passes through the esophageal hiatus at T10.
rationales.d: Greater and lesser splanchnic nerves pierce the crura rather than pass behind the medial arcuate ligament.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q005.takeaway: The esophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10, together with the vagal trunks.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q005.displayText:
The esophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10, together with the vagal trunks.

The esophageal hiatus is at the T10 vertebral level and forms the diaphragmatic constriction of the esophagus. The source lists contents of the hiatus as the esophagus, vagal trunks, gastric nerves, esophageal branches of the left gastric vessels and some lymphatics. It also gives the normal esophageal constrictions measured from the upper incisors: cricopharyngeus at 15 cm, aortic arch at 22.5 cm, left bronchus at 27.5 cm and diaphragmatic opening at 37.5 cm.
emphasis: The esophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10, together with the vagal trunks

rationales.a: T8 is the caval opening for the IVC.
rationales.b: T9 is not the conventional esophageal hiatus level.
rationales.d: T12 is the aortic hiatus level.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q006.takeaway: The aortic hiatus at T12 transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and often the azygos vein.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q006.displayText:
The aortic hiatus at T12 transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and often the azygos vein.

The aortic hiatus transmits the thoracic aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct. The source also reviews aortic dissection as an intimal tear with severe tearing interscapular pain; extension into the abdominal aorta can produce abdominal pain. CT or MRI can demonstrate the dissection, and management depends on classification and may include aggressive antihypertensive therapy or open/endovascular intervention.
emphasis: The aortic hiatus at T12 transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and often the azygos vein

rationales.a: The left gastric vein is not a structure traversing the aortic hiatus.
rationales.b: Right vagal trunk passes through the esophageal hiatus at T10.
rationales.d: Left vagal trunk also travels through the esophageal hiatus, not aortic hiatus.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q007.takeaway: The aortic hiatus transmits the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct, but the vagal trunks use the esophageal hiatus.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q007.displayText:
The aortic hiatus transmits the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct, but the vagal trunks use the esophageal hiatus.

The structure marked A is the aortic opening. The vagal trunks do not pass through the aortic opening; they pass through the esophageal hiatus at T10. The aortic opening transmits the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct.
emphasis: The aortic hiatus transmits the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct, but the vagal trunks use the esophageal hiatus

rationales.a: The aorta passes posterior to the median arcuate ligament through the aortic hiatus.
rationales.b: The azygos vein commonly passes through the aortic hiatus.
rationales.c: The thoracic duct passes through the aortic hiatus.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q008.takeaway: The left phrenic nerve descends through the diaphragm muscle anterior to the central tendon and is not a content of the esophageal hiatus.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q008.displayText:
The left phrenic nerve descends through the diaphragm muscle anterior to the central tendon and is not a content of the esophageal hiatus.

The left phrenic nerve is least likely to be injured while enlarging the esophageal hiatus because it does not pass through a diaphragmatic opening; it traverses the muscular part of the diaphragm anterior to the central tendon. The esophageal hiatus contains the esophagus, vagal trunks, gastric nerves, branches of the left gastric vessels and some lymphatics. The source notes transhiatal/Orringer esophagectomy for lower-third esophageal carcinoma, with abdominal mobilization of the stomach/lower esophagus and cervical access to the upper esophagus.
emphasis: The left phrenic nerve descends through the diaphragm muscle anterior to the central tendon and is not a content of the esophageal hiatus

rationales.a: Left gastric artery branches may enter the stomach via the esophageal hiatus region and can be at risk.
rationales.b: The right vagal trunk passes through the esophageal hiatus.
rationales.c: The left vagal trunk also traverses the hiatus and may be injured.

marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q009.takeaway: The greater splanchnic nerve pierces the crus; the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct pass posterior to the diaphragm through the aortic hiatus.
marrow__ANAT_CH44_Q009.displayText:
The greater splanchnic nerve pierces the crus; the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct pass posterior to the diaphragm through the aortic hiatus.

The greater splanchnic nerve does not pass posterior to the diaphragmatic crus; it pierces the crus to enter the abdomen. The aortic hiatus lies behind the crura and transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein.
emphasis: The greater splanchnic nerve pierces the crus; the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct pass posterior to the diaphragm through the aortic hiatus

rationales.a: The aorta passes posterior to the diaphragm at the aortic hiatus.
rationales.b: The azygos vein can accompany aorta and duct through the hiatus.
rationales.c: The thoracic duct traverses the aortic hiatus posterior to the diaphragm.
